megan: Quick sync: we need a decision for Deployments form error UX. Two proposals: progressive inline hints as users edit vs a single post-submit summary that anchors to problematic sections. Thoughts? sam: I'm pro-progressive inline for forms where users edit a bunch of fields in one go. Feels faster to recover. But for very long or paginated forms a single summary reduces visual noise. elaine: Hybrid option: show lightweight inline flags as users touch fields, but for cross-field rules (eg start/end date or quota totals) surface a summary banner that groups those. Keeps immediacy + a single place for multi-field failures. vik: Implementation notes: keep inline messages low-friction (small footnote copy) and avoid layout shift. Use aria-live="polite" for inline hints and role="alert" on the summary. Example summary markup: ```html

3 errors — please review

  • Name is required
  • Quota mismatch in Section B
``` jo: Accessibility: announce the banner first, then move focus to the summary container. After that, the first anchor can be focused. For screen readers include a concise count ("3 errors"). Avoid duplicate announcements if inline messages already were announced. karen: Required markers: I still prefer showing a subtle "Required" badge for fields that are mandatory. For compact views we can visually show a small asterisk but provide a sr-only (screen-reader-only) "Required" label that is read aloud. megan: Copy micro-decisions: prefer action-oriented errors ("Enter a name to continue") over sterile lines ("This field is required"). But keep the visible label short if space is tight. We can wire an accessibility hint that expands on demand. sam: On destructive flows: undo snackbar vs typed confirmation? My take: allow undo for reversible deletes (soft delete) with an undo toast; require typed-confirm for irreversible changes (delete org, purge logs). elaine: Agree. Let's define a threshold doc: reversible = can be recovered within 30 days via UI; irreversible = cannot be recovered or has compliance implications => typed-confirm. vik: Practical typed-confirm pattern: require user to type the resource short-id (not just "DELETE"), and keep the confirm button disabled until it matches. Example JS idea: ```js // simple match check const expected = resourceName.toLowerCase(); confirmInput.addEventListener('input', e => { confirmBtn.disabled = e.target.value.trim().toLowerCase() !== expected; }); ``` jo: UX for mobile: avoid forcing big scroll jumps when focusing errors. Use `element.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })` and prefer subtle focus ring rather than auto-scrolling the whole page. Also ensure keyboard-only users can tab the banner links. karen: One more: dedupe error surfaces. If we show inline messages, the top banner should summarize and link, but not repeat verbose text. Keep the banner terse. megan: Action items: - Elaine: produce two mocks (progressive-inline + hybrid with summary) in Figma - Vik: prototype confirm modal with typed-match + undo snackbar demo - Jo: draft a11y checklist for both patterns (announcements, focus, aria props) - Sam: draft threshold doc for undo vs typed-confirm ux-bot: Figma file started by megan: https://figma.com/file/abc123 (comments open). megan: Thanks all I'll post the mocks in the thread when ready and tag reviewers.
